actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

inputs.description: Seed used by the next reset
inputs.name: seed

facts.text: Genesis-HVelocity-G1-v0 is registered with the entry point genesislab.envs:ManagerBasedRlEnv
ManagerBasedRlEnv subclasses ManagerBasedGenesisEnv and keeps its reset/step semantics
The environment is vectorized: is_vector_env is True and metadata declares render modes
step(action) returns (observations, rewards, terminations, time-outs and info)
The scene physics timestep is dt = 0.005 s
The control step is decimation 4 physics steps
The G1 asset is the 29-DOF MJCF g1_29dof_rev_1_0.xml with control_dofs None (all DOF)
The joint position action is scaled by 0.25 and uses the default joint offset
The policy observation terms are concatenated into one group
A reset with a seed calls seed(seed), which sets cfg.seed and seeds torch and Python random
The observation is a dict of tensors and a step returns five signals
The environment assigns a torch zeros tensor to action_space and leaves observation_space None
GenesisLab is built on top of the Genesis physics engine

determinism.notes: reset(seed) calls the environment's seed(), which sets cfg.seed and seeds torch and Python random; the bridge repeats a trajectory for one seed from a fresh world. The fake uses only Python's random.Random, so a seed gives different trajectories on the fake and upstream.

gaps: the upstream action_space is a torch zeros tensor and observation_space is None, not Gymnasium spaces; the fake supplies an unbounded 29-element placeholder Box so the bridge can shape a joint-position action vector, and the real action width is resolved from the robot's actuator layout
the fake backend is a deterministic kinematic stand-in: it has no Genesis physics, contacts, actuators, sensors, terrain, events or noise model, and its observation and state values are test data
the environment is vectorized (num_envs 4096 by default) and GPU-backed; the bridge steps one action vector and the fake models one world
no snapshot or restore is offered: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state pair
the upstream environment was never run here: torch, the Genesis engine and the robot assets are not installed, so the fake and the registration were not compared with a real rollout

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the world state is kept and stays readable
